# order: EO:2206  (WPA 1944: 1915 June 1)
# WPA summary: Mrs. F. Pierard made eligiblefor appointment as a seam stressor flagmaker at the Mare Island Navy Yard, Calif.,without re gard to CivilService Rules or Navy Yard Regulations. 1915 CSR 126.
# book: Thirty-second Annual Report of the United States Civil Service Commission, fiscal year ended June 30, 1915
# scanned image 133, printed page 126; page lines 30-41
# source: https://archive.org/download/annualreportuni01commgoog/annualreportuni01commgoog_djvu.xml  sha256 92d8549007f776879ba70597db655a8e2deb53a49329d0574b35f0591c6fb041
# found by: date_and_subject; date 1915-06-01; words pierard|flagmaker|mare
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury, in view
of the faithful aJid meritorious services of her deceased husband in the Government
service, and also in view of the fact that Mrs. Ramage is without means of support.
June 1, 1915.
Mrs. F. Pierard may be appointed as seamstress or flagmaker at the navy yard,
Mare Island, Cal., without reference to the civil service rules or navy yard regulations.
Mrs. Pierard 's nusband was chief gunner's mate on the submarine F-4, which was
lost in Honolulu Harbor, leaving her to support two smaU children and an invalid
sister whose husband was lost on the F-4.
This order is recommended by the Secretary of the Navy with the concmience of
the Civil Service Commission.
June 10, 1915.
